brief: Goldman's David Mericle revises his Fed call after October core CPI surprised to the upside at +0.30%, a third straight month of hotter-than-expected inflation, broad-based and not solely an oil pass-through; Goldman estimates this implies a 35bp increase in core PCE for October. Goldman adds a third 25bp hike in March 2027, pushing the peak funds rate to 4.25-4.50% and delaying the first cut to December 2027 from September 2027; the terminal rate forecast stays at 3.25-3.50%, with further cuts in March, June and September 2028. Governor Waller's baseline is a 25bp December hike, but he said a 50bp hike should be considered if core CPI prints at 0.3% or higher, arguing 25bp risks Fed credibility; Goldman thinks most voters will resist 50bp but expects the recent prints to push most FOMC participants to signal a third hike in the December dot plot, needing only two more participants to raise their forecasts. Goldman sees the third hike landing in March rather than January, since it expects softer inflation in November/December before a "January effect" pushes prices firmer again, and still expects inflation meaningfully lower by end-2027 as oil, tariff and AI price pressures fade.
